comparison: Both strongly support the superiority of reshaped RP models (C3, C23, C31-C34). OpenEval provides detailed technical analysis of comparative data, while peer reviewers affirm this as a main contribution with 'clear visual presentations.' High agreement on this core finding.

Both support homeostatic constraint benefits (C4, C24, C39-C42). OpenEval focuses on comparative performance data across initializations, while peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as the second main contribution, praising the integration of statistical modeling and synaptic homeostasis. Strong concordance.

OpenEval evaluates synaptic normalization and firing rate regulation (C5, C46-C50) separately, while peer reviewers group these homeostatic effects together with C4 claims. Both support the findings, but OpenEval provides more granular analysis of the normalization mechanism.

Perfect agreement on dual functional role claims (C7, C60-C62). Both treat these as interpretive conclusions well-supported by the data. OpenEval notes these are inferences from computational models; peer reviewers affirm the relationship between homeostasis, representations, and accuracy is convincingly demonstrated.

Both support threshold and λ-dependent findings (C35, C37). OpenEval notes lack of theoretical justification for λ=1 default, while peer reviewers offer alternative interpretation that λ regulates average firing rate, providing additional mechanistic perspective. Agreement on validity with different emphases.

Complete agreement on synthetic data and connectivity findings (C51-C55). OpenEval notes the surprising equivalence of random and true connectivity but flags limited generalizability; peer reviewers accept these as supporting biological plausibility without raising concerns about limitations.

Perfect alignment on homeostatic variant robustness (C56-C58). Both support the similar performance across mechanisms and accept this as evidence for universal role of homeostasis. OpenEval notes unclear mechanistic explanation for convergence; peer reviewers emphasize biological plausibility implications.

Both rate C6 as UNCERTAIN with similar concerns. OpenEval notes the comparison is limited to RP framework models, not standard backpropagation networks. Peer reviewers observe that backprop models may actually outperform reshaped models slightly. Strong concordance on uncertainty about this claim.

Both support biological plausibility claims (C63-C65). OpenEval acknowledges these are supported but notes the unresolved feedback signal issue. Peer reviewers affirm this as 'important contribution to biologically plausible theory' without raising the feedback concern. Agreement on support with different attention to limitations.

Both support background and foundational claims (C1, C2, C20-C22, C26-C27). OpenEval verifies these are accurate representations of cited work; peer reviewers accept these as established prior work. Complete agreement that these provide appropriate context.
OpenEval evaluates decorrelation and efficient coding connection (C43) as supported by established theory. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific theoretical interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates mathematical interpretation of normalization and hypothesis about artificial networks (C66-C67) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details and data sources (C29, C68-C71, C76) as adequately documented for reproducibility. Peer reviewers do not provide separate evaluation of these methodological claims.
